rics.description: Foreign currency reserves, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: Foreign Currency Reserves, MoM change — month-over-month change in FX reserves.
rics.how_to_use: Sharp negative MoM (>3% drawdown) signals heavy FX intervention. Pair with IDR/USD performance for intervention-intensity signal.

rics.description: Foreign currency reserves, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: Foreign Currency Reserves, YoY change — annual pace of FX reserves accumulation/depletion.
rics.how_to_use: Tracks structural reserve position. Surges during commodity-export booms (BI accumulates); depletion during EM-stress episodes.

rics.meaning: Foreign Currency Reserves (Standardized) — companion to aIDFXRES at standardized framing. The FX-only component of total reserves.
rics.how_to_use: Use for cross-country comparisons. Indonesia FX reserves cover ~6 months of imports — comfortable per IMF adequacy metrics.

rics.description: Official international reserves, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: Official International Reserves, MoM change — month-over-month change in total reserves (FX + gold + IMF position + SDRs).
rics.how_to_use: Highest-frequency reserves trend signal. Most-watched data point each first Friday when BI releases.

rics.description: Official international reserves, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: Official International Reserves, YoY change — annual pace of total reserves accumulation.
rics.how_to_use: Smooths out monthly volatility. Indonesia reserves typically grow 3-7% pa during normal cycles; depletion in EM-stress years (-5 to -15%).

rics.meaning: Official International Reserves — total foreign exchange reserves held by Bank Indonesia. Includes FX assets, gold, IMF position, and SDRs. Published monthly (typically first Friday) by BI.
rics.how_to_use: Critical for IDR defense. Recent levels ~$140-150B, providing ~6 months of import cover (vs IMF safe minimum of 3 months). Sharp drawdowns (>$5B in a month) signal heavy FX intervention to defend IDR — historically marks IDR weakness peaks. Build-ups during commodity surpluses absorbed via BI's FX purchases.

rics.meaning: Reserves — alternative release of total international reserves. Same as aIDCRESA at different vintage.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever has fresher data; methodology and timing differences are typically minor.

rics.meaning: Foreign currency reserves — the FX-only component of total international reserves (excludes gold, IMF position, SDRs). The most actively-managed portion of BI reserves.
rics.how_to_use: ~95% of total reserves. Composition: ~60% USD, ~20% EUR, ~10% JPY/CNY (BI does not publish exact split). Drawn down for FX intervention; replenished via commodity-export FX accumulation. Pair with monthly IDR/USD performance for intervention intensity signal.

rics.meaning: Reserves, International — alternative release of total international reserves.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever has fresher data; methodology differences across releases are typically minor and resolved on revision.

rics.description: Reserves, Reserve in foreign exchange, currency and deposits
rics.meaning: Reserves: Foreign Exchange, Currency and Deposits — the FX cash + bank deposits component of reserves. Most-liquid portion, used for daily FX operations and short-term IDR defense.
rics.how_to_use: Subset of aIDFXRES (which also includes securities held in custody). The currency/deposits portion is the immediately-deployable defense buffer. Tracks BI's day-to-day FX intervention capacity.

rics.meaning: Reserves: Reserve Others — non-FX, non-gold, non-IMF residual reserve assets. Small.
rics.how_to_use: Niche. Captures other-claims items not classified into FX/gold/SDR/IMF position.

rics.description: Reserves, Reserve position in the fund
rics.meaning: Reserves: Reserve Position in the Fund — Indonesia's reserve tranche position at the IMF. Funds Indonesia can withdraw on demand without conditions.
rics.how_to_use: Niche. Used in BoP accounting; rarely activated. Small relative to FX reserves (~$1B vs ~$140B FX).

rics.meaning: Reserves: Reserve Total — same conceptual measure as aIDCRESA (total international reserves) at potentially different release vintage.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever has fresher data. The standardized aIDCRESA aligns with IMF SDDS reporting standards.

rics.meaning: Gold reserves component of international reserves. Bank Indonesia holds ~78 metric tons of gold (small relative to reserve-currency central banks).
rics.how_to_use: Slow-moving. Stock unchanged for years; valuation moves with gold price (USD per troy ounce). Larger central banks (China, India, Russia) have been net gold buyers post-2020; BI has been broadly neutral. Useful for tracking total-reserve composition trends but not actively managed.

rics.meaning: Reserves: SDR Holdings — Special Drawing Rights at the IMF. Reserve asset created by IMF; valued by basket of major currencies (USD, EUR, CNY, JPY, GBP).
rics.how_to_use: Boosted in August 2021 IMF general SDR allocation ($650B globally; Indonesia received ~$6.3B). Stable since. Useful for tracking IMF reserve operations but not actively managed.
